overall.summary: All 193 claims and every prose number reproduce (L1 clean), but one sentence in the Combined day and evening bill part attributes to that part an interaction that comes from the Heavy daytime use part; three sentences are weakened (a hinge point that contradicts its own example, a direction that reverses at 4+ service calls, and two L4 wording issues).

findings.statement: It also rises more for customers without voice-mail messages: from about 2% to about 11%, against about 1% to about 2% for a typical customer with messages (and so a voice-mail plan).
findings.check: probe the typical customer with a voice-mail plan, day charge 19.07 and 42.40, messages 0 and 17; read the ann_89 contribution. Compare with C116's own difference-in-differences through the part.
findings.evidence: Inside ann_89 the day-charge effect is the same with and without messages: contribution -0.552 -> -0.316 (+0.236) at 0 messages and -0.071 -> +0.165 (+0.236) at 17 messages. C116's own through-part difference-in-differences is -0.077 log-odds against -1.380 for the whole model (about 6%). The 2%->11% vs 1%->2% numbers are identical to C103 (ann_88): the gap comes from the voice-mail plan switching off hinge 3460 in ann_88 (ann_89 does not read the voice-mail plan). The sentence describes another part's mechanism.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold typical --set 'voice mail plan=1' --sweep 'total day charge=19.07:42.4:5' --sweep 'number vmail messages=0,17'
uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --claim C116

findings.statement: A higher daytime charge lowers it steadily up to about 15.64 US dollars (between 7.93 and 31.04 for different customers), then no further: ... from about 11% at 19.07 US dollars to about 2% at 42.40 US dollars
findings.check: probe the claim's reference case (3 calls, 158 day minutes) sweeping day charge 10 to 46
findings.evidence: For the sentence's own typical customer the ann_90 contribution falls steadily from +2.94 at $10 to +0.08 at $31 and is flat (+0.071) from $34 on: the flattening is at about $31.5 (the claim's typical_hinge 31.54), not $15.64. 15.64 is the median fold across customers (from C097). Read literally, the sentence says nothing changes above $15.64 and then gives a fall from 11% to 2% between $19 and $42. Direction and risk numbers reproduce.

findings.statement: Higher daytime minutes raise it ..., and even more so with at most one service call: from about 2% to about 9% with at most one call, and from about 6% to about 9% with more calls.
findings.check: probe the typical customer at 126 min/$21.42 and 236 min/$40.12, calls 1, 2, 4
findings.evidence: Raises at 1 call (2.3% -> 7.1%) and 2 calls (2.9% -> 7.1%), but at 4 calls higher daytime use lowers the risk: 35.9% at 126 minutes vs 14.9% at 236 minutes (ann_90 +3.15 -> +0.78). C059's own group mean through the part for 'more than 1 call' is -0.26 log-odds (lowers on average). 'Raise ... with more calls' holds only for 2 calls; the reversal is raised in worth_checking[0] but not here.
